quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to create a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, you must slow down and create a clear path for the emergency vehicle, then stop. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving, regardless of warnings on the label.
Drive only during daylight.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Before driving, check the label for warnings about cold medicine, allergy pills, or other drugs. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while taking medication.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Stay close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull off the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to let others know you are there.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking, which could cause a car behind you to hit your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes poor.
You become less alert.
You relax and can focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You relax and can focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, hurts your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to see in bright headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be ready to stop?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What is a possible penalty for a first driving under the influence offense?

options.text: Three years in state prison and a $3,000 fine
Three months in county jail
Two months in county jail and a $30 fine
Six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine

questions.correctAnswerText: Six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine
questions.explanation: For a first DUI conviction, penalties can include up to $1,000 in fines, up to six months in jail, and license suspension for up to 45 days. Higher penalties apply if a child is endangered, someone is injured, or someone dies.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic light is broken.
You do not need to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams point upward and bounce off fog, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always obey speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When must you pull over to let an emergency vehicle pass?

options.text: Regardless of your direction.
Only if it is following you.
Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Pull over to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time allows a person to recover from the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look into the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if you get stranded in a snowstorm?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. You are easier to find if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: If there is no stop line at an intersection where you must stop, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve ahead.
Turn right or left.
Traffic can only go in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic can only go in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign tells drivers that traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. At higher speeds, you can see less around you. You must stay alert to dangers because of this reduced vision.

questions.question: You cannot drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must follow the posted speed limit and drive at a speed that is safe. Consider traffic, weather, road conditions, light, and pedestrians. Adjust your speed to match all these factors.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit can:

options.text: Make you a very safe driver.
Always give you the right-of-way.
Mean other cars should not pass you.
Create unsafe driving conditions.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let other cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when needed for safety.

questions.question: Someone is injured in an accident you caused. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Never move the injured person.
Do not move them unless needed. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless needed. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.
